messages:
anne-ops: :rotating_light: seeing a sudden perf cliff on inference-prod-3 around 11:07 UTC. 95th latency up 6x, error rate for long-chat routes spiking. Console shows cont-batcher queue length >> normal.

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2076543210 - continuous-batching surge on inference-prod-3. Severity: P1. Pager notified.

mike-sre: pulling traces now. Early signal: kvcache eviction rate jumped and mem pressure on the serving node. Looks like very large batches consuming the KV paging window.

leah-ml: on the model side: recent rollout of cb config v2 pushed earlier today. Config has max_num_seqs=512 and max_batch_tokens=65536. That feels high for this workload. Was supposed to be 64 / 16384.

chris-support: customers impacted: AcmePayments and NimbusSearch reporting timeouts (~30s) and 429s. Support is triaging.

anne-ops: good find. hypothesis: misconfigured continuous-batching params caused huge batches -> huge KV cache pages -> eviction storm -> higher latency and OOMs on some workers. Need quick mitigation: revert config or patch to safe defaults.

mike-sre: agree. I'm going to patch the cont-batcher config in prod to conservative values and roll canary to a subset of workers.

mike-sre: running patch (kubectl apply) now:
```
kubectl -n inference set configmap cont-batcher-config --from-file=config.yaml=<(cat <<'YAML'
max_num_seqs: 64
max_batch_tokens: 16384
batch_timeout_ms: 25
allow_long_tail: false
YAML
)
```

deploy-bot: deploy triggered: cont-batcher-config v2.1 -> rolling update on node pool inference-prod-3-canary (2 pods).

anne-ops: canary observing... mike, add throttle on KV paging if possible (limit concurrent page reads) so we don't re-create thrash mid-rollout.

mike-sre: added a temporary circuit on paging: paging.max_concurrent_reads=8 (was 64) via runtime feature flag.

leah-ml: monitoring shows canary workers' batch sizes drop from median ~420 seqs to ~30 seqs. KV eviction rate drops 80% in canary.

chris-support: AcmePayments reported partial recovery for a few requests (from 28s -> 600ms) after the canary. Still some timeouts in non-canary nodes. Sending customer note: "we've identified a batching config regression and are rolling a fix; partial recovery observed".

anne-ops: rolling to remainder of pool now. Steps: 1) set safe config, 2) ramp feature flag for paging throttle, 3) monitor 95/99 latencies + KV eviction metric.

mike-sre: rolling update in progress. Patch will take ~6 min to hit all pods. Watching metrics.

oncall-bot: Handoff scheduled: anne-ops -> mike-sre in 30m. Handoff channel: #incidents.

mike-sre: metrics show 95th dropped back to baseline after 4 minutes from canary start, 99th still noisy but trending down. No new OOMs.

leah-ml: logging snippet from affected worker before rollback:
```
[2026-02-14T11:05:42Z] WARN cont-batch: built batch seqs=496 tokens=48212 route=/chat/long tail=true
[2026-02-14T11:05:43Z] ERROR kvcache: page_eviction spike count=172 evict_rate=0.9
[2026-02-14T11:05:44Z] ERROR runtime: OOM minor, reclaiming cache pages
```

mike-sre: confirmed root cause is config drift. v2 config landed in production via CI job earlier and missed a review lint that should have caught out-of-bound values. I'll file a postmortem on the CI gating.

chris-support: step to customers: send follow-up explaining mitigation and ETA for full recovery. SLA impact: AcmePayments saw ~2 min total impact window; offering credits per policy.

anne-ops: quick mitigation checklist for now (keeps):
- revert unsafe cont-batcher params to known-good defaults
- add runtime guard rails to reject max_num_seqs > 256 and max_batch_tokens > 32768
- throttle KV paging concurrency when mem pressure high
- add alert for sudden jump in avg_batch_seq_count > 3x baseline

mike-sre: I've applied runtime guard and added a prometheus alert rule: cont_batch_seq_median_rate > 3*baseline for 1m -> P2. Also a hard deny on >512 in config loader.

deploy-bot: rollout complete: cont-batcher-config v2.1 deployed to 12 pods. No failures.

leah-ml: quality check: end-to-end latent sampling for affected routes shows token generation times back to normal. Embedding clients unaffected.

chris-support: AcmePayments and NimbusSearch contacted with mitigation note and follow-up. Both confirmed improved response.

anne-ops: lowering severity to P2 while we keep monitoring. We'll keep this thread open for postmortem notes. Handoff to mike-sre in 20 minutes. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

mike-sre: taking over — will maintain watch for another 60m and start a root-cause ticket (RCA-2076543210).
